claims.claim: mRNA vaccines became practical through nucleoside base modifications (Kariko and Weissman, published 2005) that nearly abolished the inflammatory innate-immune response to synthetic mRNA - work done well over a decade before the COVID-19 pandemic.
claims.episode_span: that required both modified nucleosides and a reliable lipid carrier, both of which had been under development for more than a decade before the pandemic
claims.source_title: Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2023 - NobelPrize.org
claims.supporting_quote: The results were striking: The inflammatory response was almost abolished when base modifications were included in the mRNA. This was a paradigm change in our understanding of how cells recognize and respond to different forms of mRNA. Karikó and Weissman immediately understood that their discovery had profound significance for using mRNA as therapy. These seminal results were published in 2005, fifteen years before the COVID-19 pandemic.

claims.claim: Most influenza vaccines are grown in fertilized chicken eggs, with an estimated 600 million eggs used each year for flu vaccine production.
claims.episode_span: For influenza this meant millions of fertilized eggs each season; for other viruses it meant large bioreactors running mammalian or insect cells.
claims.supporting_quote: Up to 3 eggs are needed to produce one dose of a trivalent vaccine, and an estimated 600 million eggs are produced each year for flu vaccine production.

claims.claim: First-in-human dosing of the original SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine candidate (Moderna's mRNA-1273) began in March 2020, roughly two months after development was announced in January 2020 following publication of the viral sequence.
claims.episode_span: the compression of the interval from antigen sequence publication to first-in-human dosing to roughly two months for the original SARS-CoV-2 mRNA candidates
claims.supporting_quote: In March 2020, the phase I human trial of mRNA-1273 began in partnership with the US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

claims.claim: A single mRNA vaccine dose contains micrograms of mRNA (mRNA-1273 uses 100-microgram doses).
claims.episode_span: a single vaccine dose contains micrograms of material
claims.supporting_quote: one group receiving two 100-μg doses of mRNA-1273 vaccine and the other receiving a placebo of 0.9% sodium chloride

claims.claim: Laboratory-developed vaccines (attenuated/inactivated whole-pathogen products) trace back to Louis Pasteur, who introduced the second generation of vaccines in the 1880s.
claims.episode_span: Vaccine makers inherited a process that began with Louis Pasteur and was refined through the twentieth century.
claims.supporting_quote: Following on from Jenner's work, the second generation of vaccines was introduced in the 1880s by Louis Pasteur who developed vaccines for chicken cholera and anthrax
